repair_steps: Have a qualified repairer clean the panel, inspect the scratch depth, and confirm whether it is limited to the clear coat or has exposed the colour coat, primer, or bare metal.

For a minor finish defect, use the appropriate graded abrasive to refine the damaged area, then compound and polish it; deeper paint damage requires the vehicle maker's approved primer, colour, and clear-coat refinishing process.
Clean and inspect the finished area under suitable lighting; if the scratch remains visible, exposes metal, or crosses a panel edge, refer it for professional refinishing.

parts.part_name: Mock fine abrasive and polishing kit

repair_steps: Have a qualified repairer pre-clean the panel and inspect the dent, paint condition, panel material, nearby reinforcements, and access behind the damaged area before choosing a repair method.

Use an OEM-approved paintless dent-repair method only when the paint and metal are suitable; otherwise remove the damaged finish, restore the panel contour, and apply body filler or glaze according to the repair-product and vehicle-maker procedures.
Sand and prepare the repaired area for primer and paint, then verify the panel contour, gaps, finish, and refitted trim during the final inspection.

parts.part_name: Mock body filler and applicator kit

repair_steps: Have a qualified repairer clean the area, remove trim as required, and inspect both sides of the panel to determine whether corrosion is superficial or has perforated or structurally weakened the metal.

Remove the affected coating and corrosion to sound metal using the approved abrasive and repair process; perforated or weakened metal must be repaired or replaced using the vehicle maker's body-repair instructions.
Restore the specified primer, paint, seam sealer, cavity protection, and undercoating as applicable, then inspect the completed repair for full coverage and corrosion protection.
